$comment: The masking cases both implementations must answer identically. They lived inline in tools/test-masking.mjs, which made the JavaScript the only thing that had to satisfy them; a port could then agree with the prose in docs/contracts/masking.md and disagree with the code. Every entry names its expected displayValue and resulting policy, so a degradation is stated rather than inferred.
$degradesComment: Too short to mask without half-revealing. The result must say fully_masked: what happened, not what was attempted.

degrades.why: 3 code points would leave only 1 hidden
7 code points is below the token minimum of 8
a single-code-point local part reveals itself

$boundariesComment: One code point longer than the cases above: these must NOT degrade, or the minimum is really the minimum plus one.
$minimumHiddenComment: No policy but structural_label may leave fewer than two code points hidden. Every short value under every policy is checked, because the rule is about all of them and a table naming a few would leave the rest unstated.
